title: Spatial-DC maps a candidate fibroblast–cancer signaling interaction in pancreatic tumors
summary: Spatial-DC reconstructed cell-type-resolved spatial proteomes and suggested COL8A1–ITGA2 communication between cancer-associated fibroblasts and pancreatic cancer cells. Multiplexed immunohistochemistry supported the spatial predictions; human protein co-expression was associated with survival. The pairing was already known: the result concerns its inferred spatial deployment, not a new receptor pair or established causal mechanism. This record uses the May 27, 2026 journal version; the result already appeared in the December 20, 2024 preprint.
organization: Southern University of Science and Technology; Tencent AI for Life Sciences Laboratory

evidence.tested: Retrospective spatial proteomic reconstruction and human survival association. Same-study multiplexed immunohistochemistry supports spatial distributions and co-expression, not causal COL8A1–ITGA2 communication.
evidence.unknown: No causal signaling perturbation, therapeutic benefit or independent replication is established in the reviewed material. Current review read indexed publisher introduction and NLM abstract/metadata; full journal methods were inaccessible. Earlier primary preprint XML was read in the project audit on November 16, 2026; revised journal quantitative details were not assessed.
evidence.ai_role: Graph-enhanced transfer learning deconvolved mixed spots and reconstructed cell-type-resolved protein profiles used to infer spatial interactions.
